entries.source: SDK 26.2, AVPlayerItem+MediaPlayerAdditions.h, @interface AVPlayerItem (MPAdditions) / @property (nonatomic, copy, nullable) NSDictionary<NSString *, id> *nowPlayingInfo MP_API(ios(16.0), tvos(16.0))
entries.reason: this row waited two turns for the rung that can decide it, because its owner class is AVFoundation's and not MediaPlayer's: the per-image read (tools/mach32_methods.py over the MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000, 236 classes, 41 categories) cannot see AVPlayerItem at all, and the release's whole-cache SELECTOR LIST cannot decide it either - nowPlayingInfo is on ONE of its 113981 distinct names, because some class somewhere declares it, which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. The rung that decides a member is the whole cache, read through coordination/heavy.sh at a load of 9.08: CHARON_ROOT=<worktree> xmake l tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua ~/.charon/dyld/6.1.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7, 12549 lines = 11378 classes and 1171 protocols. From that read AVPlayerItem lives in AVFoundation.framework/AVFoundation with 237 own instance selectors and 35 own class: status, timedMetadata, duration and MPAVItem ARE among the 237 - MPAVItem being the MediaPlayer category's own method - and nowPlayingInfo and setNowPlayingInfo: are NOT. One class, one reader, a YES and a NO. Across the WHOLE cache exactly two classes declare nowPlayingInfo in their own instance list, MPNowPlayingInfoCenter and PrivateFrameworks/MediaRemote's MRMediaRemoteState; neither is AVPlayerItem. A class no framework has reads absent from the same file, so the reader is not answering YES to everything. So the release carries neither the accessor nor the class-side property on this class. THE LINK, and it is a structural consequence of the same fact rather than a second one: a category's class reference is a symbol, so the band that builds this object has to name AVFoundation or ld leaves _OBJC_CLASS_$_AVPlayerItem undefined - measured, the 6.1.3 armv7 band failing with Undefined symbols for architecture armv7 on exactly that name from __OBJC_$_CATEGORY_AVPlayerItem_$_CharonMPAdditions. MediaPlayerBackports declared MediaPlayer, UIKit and Foundation only, and every other object in that folder is a MediaPlayer or UIKit class, so this row is the only one that needed the fourth. AVFoundation is now in that list (modules/apple/backports.lua), which binds the category to the RELEASE's own AVPlayerItem rather than to anything this port defines, and which costs no image: the band links -framework MediaPlayer anyway and the release's own libMediaPlayer already loads AVFoundation - otool -L on ~/.charon/dyld/6.1.3/MediaPlayer, the file that release ships beside its shared cache, 39 LC_LOAD_DYLIB entries including /System/Library/Frameworks/AVFoundation.framework/AVFoundation (compatibility version 1.0.0, current version 2.0.0). Re-homing the property onto MPNowPlayingInfoCenter was rejected as a change in behaviour, not a fix: the header declares it on AVPlayerItem, so a caller writes [playerItem setNowPlayingInfo:] and nothing on MPNowPlayingInfoCenter would answer that.
entries.effect: a dictionary that copies on set and reads back what was set, nil when nothing was set - the header's own nullability and `copy`. OBJC_ASSOCIATION_COPY_NONATOMIC, so a caller that mutates the dictionary it passed cannot reach into the item's value, as Apple's own synthesised setter cannot be reached either. On a release where the system reads this property it fills it in; on this one there is no system reader, so the value is what the caller stored - a nowPlayingInfo synthesised from the item's timedMetadata would be inventing an answer Apple's own accessor does not produce here. STORAGE: a CATEGORY on a class AVFoundation owns, so no ivar can be added and the value is an associated object, public API and what this tree already does for the same problem (WebKit/WKWebpagePreferences13.m:39-42, SensorKit/SRSensorReader.m:120-135)
